key_insight: A UPML-truncated CIP-FEM for 2D Helmholtz obstacle scattering is shown to be stable and accurate with explicit wavenumber dependence, including preasymptotic error control.
engineering_relevance: The result provides a practical high-frequency scattering solver with provable performance and reduced truncation error for finite element simulations.
method: Derive wavenumber-explicit stability using stretched Green kernel estimates for the Cartesian complex-coordinate PML.
Prove the truncated UPML inf-sup constant scales like O(k^-1) in a k-weighted H1 norm and the PML truncation error decays exponentially.
Establish piecewise H^{1+s} regularity to support preasymptotic error bounds for the CIP-FEM.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical stability/error bounds and numerical experiments that confirm the predictions in the high-frequency regime.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on handling coefficient jumps and corner singularities in the PML domain, which can affect mesh design and implementation.
paper_title: Wavenumber-explicit stability and preasymptotic error analysis of UPML finite element method for obstacle scattering problems
